## Design ground motions

Seismic ground motions will be affected by the geotechnical and dynamic characteristics of the different soil layers overlying the bedrock. The procedure by which the ground motions at the surface level are determined is known as the dynamic site response. The site response spectra must be obtained for the specific geotechnical conditions of the foundation soil of each project facility. The ASCE/SEI 7-22 Standard {@ASCE722} provides guidelines for conducting geotechnical investigations and includes a site classification system that categorises sites into classes based on their soil properties, such as shear wave velocity, depth to bedrock, and soil type.  Further details of soil classification system can be found in @sec-SC_ASCE722 and @sec-SC_AS1170

For rock and hard soils site conditions (site class A, B, and BC soils), it can be assumed that the ground has virtually no effect on the frequency content of seismic ground motions. For Site Class E or F soils, the site response must be obtained from a site-specific dynamic (time-history) analysis according to ASCE/SEI 7-22 [-@ASCE722] Section 21.1. For Site Class C, CD, D, and DE soils, spectral ordinates $S_a(T_n)^{sc}$ can be obtained from an multi-period amplification factor $F(T_n,v_S)$ in terms of shear-wave velocities $\bar v_S$. Further details of MPAF methodology can be found in @sec-MPAF . 

> Based on geophysical studies conducted at the `r params$project` site, the following site conditions have been identified:  A scenario of medium to hard rocks with shear-wave velocities $\bar v_S$ ranging 900-1100 m/s, which classify as site class B

The site response spectra are obtained from the combination of the rock response spectra with the multiple period amplification factors, as established in ASCE/SEI 7-22.
